en: On the shore of the ocean of milk, where the sand shines with pure gems, Mukunda sits on a seat made of pearl garlands, his body adorned with pearls clear as crystal. White clouds above him pour down nectar, and he is full of joy. May he, who holds the discus, lotus, mace and conch, purify us.

first: भूः पादौ यस्य नाभिर्वियदसुरनिलश्चन्द्रसूर्यौ च नेत्रे
en: The earth is his feet, the sky his navel, the wind his breath, the moon and sun his eyes, the directions his ears, heaven his head, fire his mouth, and the ocean his belly. Inside him the whole universe plays, with gods, humans, birds, cattle, serpents, Gandharvas and demons. I bow to Vishnu, the Lord whose body is the three worlds.

Om. I bow to Vishnu: peaceful in form, lying on the serpent, with a lotus at his navel, lord of the gods, support of the universe, vast like the sky, dark like a cloud, with a beautiful body. He is the beloved of Lakshmi, lotus-eyed, reached by yogis in meditation, the remover of the fear of worldly life, the one Lord of all the worlds.

I bow to Vishnu, the one Lord of all the worlds: dark like a rain cloud, dressed in yellow silk, marked with the Shrivatsa, his body shining with the Kaustubha gem, full of holiness, with long lotus eyes.
Salutation to Vishnu, the mighty one, the first of all beings, the support of the earth, who takes many forms.
I bow my head to the four-armed Vishnu, with conch and discus, crown and earrings, yellow clothes and lotus eyes, his chest shining with a garland and the Kaustubha gem.

I take refuge in Krishna, seated on a golden throne in the shade of the Parijata tree, dark like a cloud, with long eyes, richly adorned, with a moon-like face and four arms, the Shrivatsa mark on his chest, together with Rukmini and Satyabhama.
